source: The peers endpoint’s answers, as GET /api/companies/{ticker}/peers?metric={metric} serves them (PeerComparisonResponse, backend/app/schemas/peers.py), each case labelled with the metric its request named. The two production cases are production’s own entries: the pair joined from JPM’s and BAC’s single-company answers, and the single as JPM served it; every other case is synthetic, its companies and figures invented for the case. Each envelope is computed as backend/app/services/peers_service.py computes it: value descending with the ticker as tie-break and withheld values last, competition ranks and percentile round(below / (m − 1) × 100, 1) over the companies with a value, peer_count the entries, subject the subject’s own entry, or one synthesised where the subject holds no fact. backend/tests/unit/test_peers_fixture_contract.py seeds every case and holds the service to it.

pair.case: production: JPM’s and BAC’s single-company answers of 2026-10-31 08:35 UTC (GET /api/companies/{JPM,BAC}/peers, each sic null and peer_count 1), joined into the pair the service answers for JPM once both hold SIC 6021 (the committed census’s code, unverified against EDGAR): each entry as served, ranked and counted as the service would

spread.case: synthetic: eleven companies spread from $416.0B to $5.1B, the subject sixth, so a phone opens mid-plot; two five-glyph tickers, one with a dot (as GOOGL and BRK.B, the committed universe’s widest), and one company a fiscal year ahead; every company and figure invented

spread, subject first.case: synthetic: the spread’s eleven companies with the first, MEGAX, the subject, a sector’s largest company: its column’s centred scroll falls before the scroll’s start, so a plot that scrolls opens there, on its own axis with no sticky gutter; every company and figure invented

spread, subject tenth.case: synthetic: the spread’s eleven companies with the tenth, MCRX, the subject: on a phone its column’s centred scroll runs past the scroll’s end, so the plot opens at that end, its column in view; every company and figure invented

near-equal.case: synthetic: eleven near-equal companies, $4.85B to $4.95B, the dense case lessons/frontend-verify-chart-annotations-on-dense-data.md asks for; every company and figure invented

six-glyph.case: synthetic: a six-glyph ticker among nine companies (no ticker in the committed 518-ticker universe is longer than five glyphs, but the endpoint answers any company row); every company and figure invented

net margin.case: synthetic: a margin cohort, unit pure, in percentage points, each value calculated and needing review (reconciled false), as production’s margins answer; one negative; every company and figure invented

diluted EPS.case: synthetic: a per-share cohort, unit USD/shares, one loss; every company and figure invented

CNY revenue.case: synthetic: a cohort reporting in CNY, which the service ranks only against other CNY filers (its currency guard), so amounts print in CN¥; every company and figure invented

duplicate ticker.case: synthetic: two companies answering one ticker (Company.ticker is indexed, not unique; cik is), so a chart keys its slots by place, since buildBarChart refuses a key given twice; every company and figure invented

production single.case: production: JPM’s answer of 2026-10-31 08:35 UTC (GET /api/companies/JPM/peers), as served: no SIC code is stored, so the service ranks the subject alone (sic null, peer_count 1), the shape every company answers until the SIC backfill runs; the panel shows nothing

no facts.case: synthetic, in the shape USB, PNC and SCHW answered on 2026-10-31: a subject with no annual fact for the metric, so peer_count 0, a synthesised subject (value, rank and provenance null) and no peers; the panel shows nothing; the company is invented

no fact, with peers.case: synthetic: a subject with no annual revenue fact, nor a net interest income one (so the service keeps revenue), whose industry code’s other companies hold one: the shape USB, PNC and SCHW would answer once the SIC backfill gives their codes companies with a revenue fact; peer_count 3, a synthesised subject (value, rank and provenance null) and three companies ranked; the panel shows nothing; every company and figure invented

no gross profit, with peers.case: synthetic: a subject that holds no gross profit fact (a company whose income statement shows none), asked for gross profit, so a synthesised subject and the two companies of its industry code that hold one; picked in the card, the plot’s place says the subject’s figure is unavailable; every company and figure invented

withheld peer.case: synthetic: a pair whose peer’s value is withheld (a derived diluted EPS, which the service withholds), so peer_count 2 and one company with a value; the panel shows nothing; every company and figure invented

withheld subject.case: synthetic: a pair whose subject’s value is withheld (a derived diluted EPS), so peer_count 2 and one company with a value, not the subject; the panel shows nothing; every company and figure invented

withheld subject, with peers.case: synthetic: two companies with a value and a subject whose value is withheld (a derived diluted EPS), so peer_count 3 and the subject unranked; the panel shows nothing, and picked in the card the plot’s place says the subject’s figure is unavailable; every company and figure invented

peers.company_name: Synthetic Withheld With Peers A Inc
Synthetic Withheld With Peers B Corp

pair plus withheld.case: synthetic: two companies with a value, the subject second, and a third whose value is withheld (a derived diluted EPS), so peer_count 3 while the subject ranks second of two; every company and figure invented

cap.case: synthetic: fourteen companies, the subject thirteenth, so the panel draws the top ten and the subject, eleven bars, the subject last; every company and figure invented

cap, subject fifth.case: synthetic: the cap case’s fourteen companies with the fifth the subject, so the panel draws the top eleven, the subject among them, and its footnote says the chart shows the top 11 of the 14; every company and figure invented

cap, subject eleventh.case: synthetic: the cap case’s fourteen companies with the eleventh the subject, the last the eleven slots hold among the top, so the panel draws the top eleven and its footnote says the chart shows the top 11 of the 14; every company and figure invented

cap, subject twelfth.case: synthetic: the cap case’s fourteen companies with the twelfth the subject, the first past the top eleven, so the panel draws the top ten and the subject and its footnote says so, naming CAPL; every company and figure invented

cap, tie at the tenth.case: synthetic: the cap case’s fourteen companies with the tenth and eleventh tied (CAPJ and CAPK, both ranked 10) and the subject thirteenth, so the cut above the subject stops before the tie and the panel draws the top nine and the subject, its footnote saying the top 9; every company and figure invented

cap, tie at the eleventh.case: synthetic: the cap case’s first twelve companies with the eleventh and twelfth tied (CAPK and CAPL, both ranked 11) and the subject second, so the eleven slots stop before the tie and the panel draws the top ten, a slot left empty, its footnote saying the top 10 of the 12; every company and figure invented

cap, all tied.case: synthetic: twelve companies of one value, all ranked 1, the subject last in the answer’s ticker order, so no cut keeps a rank whole: the panel draws the first ten and the subject, and its footnote gives the count alone, 11 of the 12; every company and figure invented

capital expenditures.case: synthetic: a cohort ranked on capital expenditures, a concept the service answers (facts/concepts.py) and FEATURED does not name, so the panel can neither label nor format it and shows nothing, though the subject and two other companies hold a value; every company and figure invented

bank.case: synthetic: a bank that reports net interest income and no revenue, asked for revenue, so the service ranks its sector on net interest income instead (peers_service.py:58-83), as GS answered on 2026-10-31; every company and figure invented
